Cw: rape, sexual assault

Listening to people frame the current #MeToo moment in Sri Lanka as needing to have a linear and productive outcome and closure made me want to share this again. Being heard and believed is the first, and sometimes only, outcome. https://t.co/AbBvALywWF

"Acknowledging that the carceral approach of locking people up and throwing away the key is most often preferred because it absolves society of any responsibility, will enable more meaningful and honest solutions." @ambikasat #MeToo #LKA  https://t.co/N9UtR3aoby

Some of the discussions around #MeToo #lka as well as the increasingly totalising use of "civil society" (including my own) made me revisit "The Idea of Civil Society in the South: Imaginings, Transplants, Designs" by Nira Wickramasinghe. Lots to chew on. https://t.co/C0HBVIoJ2C

Thought provoking paper by Nayantara. 

“the design and affordances in the current platforms are intentional and not inevitable, and have shaped the public around #metoo, while acknowledging that users nevertheless often navigate platforms subversively and with personal agency”

I've also been thinking about the counter-narrative of cancel culture associated with #MeToo. In #LKA perpetrators continue to thrive. One won an award. Another – based outside of lka – still harasses and emotionally abuses women remotely but is platformed, esp by civil society.

On the other hand, the women who spoke up in the #MeToo #LKA moment are having a much harder time. One had to resign from her workplace. Another – a vocal champion of social justice – was accused of trying to derail a campaign (and later also bizarrely thanked for not doing so).

As I've reflected before, this moment and any that emerge in the future won't be neat or linear, and we have to stay with the pain, the catharsis and the messiness – both public and private – in order to see where these #MeToo #LKA moments take us. https://t.co/ePfbJ36SKk
